hero.title: Hi, I'm
hero.subtitle: I'm an LLM application engineer and game systems researcher: I build agents, RAG, and multi-agent systems for real problems, and I explore game design through system breakdowns and playable demos.
hero.name: Yixuan Tao

about.title: About Me
about.heading: Understanding systems, building better experiences
about.content1: I work on two tracks at once: applying large language models to real engineering problems — agents, retrieval-augmented generation, and multi-agent systems — while breaking down game systems to understand how rules shape player behavior and experience.
about.content2: During my internship I built a multimodal RAG knowledge base and a ReAct orchestration kernel for a corporate intranet, and in my spare time I ship playable game demos with Godot. I care about turning ideas into things that actually run and can be experienced.
about.content3: This site collects my AI engineering practice and game systems research — a place for ongoing writing, notes, and project iterations.

projects.title: AI Engineering × Game Design
projects.heading: Selected Projects
projects.subtitle: From agents and RAG systems to playable game demos — projects I actually built.

platform.name: Unified Enterprise Agent Platform
platform.description: An enterprise multi-agent platform combining my own components with three core capabilities from my internship — multimodal RAG, a ReAct orchestration kernel, and an EMC comparison tool.
highlights: FastAPI gateway + Next.js frontend with SSE streaming; LangGraph Supervisor orchestrates four specialist agents.
Multimodal RAG: BGE-M3 dense + BM25 sparse hybrid retrieval, RRF fusion, and reranker re-ranking with cross-modal image retrieval.
ReAct orchestration kernel with plugin-based tools and short/long-term memory; Ragas six-metric evaluation and Langfuse tracing.

itAgent.name: IT Support AI Agent
itAgent.description: An agent for internal IT support in SMEs: RAG-based knowledge Q&A, LangGraph ticket workflows, automatic Jira ticket creation, and human escalation.
highlights: Intent routing and multi-turn slot filling that auto-generates structured tickets and creates them via the Jira API.
Automatic escalation to humans when retrieval confidence is low or security-sensitive topics arise.

airstrike.name: Airstrike
airstrike.description: A 2D rocket defense game built with Godot: 20 escalating waves, five power-ups, destructible terrain, and a built-in map editor.
highlights: 20 waves of escalating difficulty with four enemy types and a CSV-driven wave config.
Five power-ups, destructible terrain, and a built-in map editor for custom levels.

chronoFront.name: Chrono Front
chronoFront.description: A card-based roguelite MVP for a game design portfolio: six heroes, 24 character cards, 12 class talents, and a three-phase boss fight. Playable right in the browser.
chronoFront.role: Personal project · Systems design and implementation
highlights: Deterministic combat rules decoupled from presentation, headless-testable; cards, heroes, and encounters fully JSON-driven.
Turn-based three-slot decisions — Engage / Clash / Finish — with public enemy intent for readable risk assessment.
Exported to the web with Godot and playable right on this site.
